+};
+
+struct _BpfJumpRef
+{
+  size_t       instruction;
+  bool         true_branch;
+  BpfLabel    *label;
+  BpfJumpRef  *next;
+};
+
+struct _BpfBuilder
+{
+  struct sock_filter *instructions;
+  size_t              len;
+  size_t              allocated;
+  BpfJumpRef         *jump_refs;
+};
+
+static uint64_t
+parse_constant (const char               *value,
+                const SeccompConstant    *constants,
+                size_t                    n_constants,
+                const char               *description)
+{
+  char *end = NULL;
+  unsigned long long parsed;
+  size_t i;
+
+  errno = 0;
+  parsed = strtoull (value, &end, 0);
+  if (value[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' && errno != ERANGE)
+    return parsed;
+
+  for (i = 0; i < n_constants; i++)
+    {
+      if (strcmp (value, constants[i].name) == 0)
+        return constants[i].value;
+    }
+
+  die ("Invalid seccomp %s: %s", description, value);
+}
+
+static int
+parse_syscall (const char *name)
+{
+  char *end = NULL;
+  unsigned long parsed;
+  size_t i;
+
+  errno = 0;
+  parsed = strtoul (name, &end, 0);
+  if (name[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' &&
+      errno != ERANGE && parsed <= INT_MAX)
+    return (int) parsed;
+
+  for (i = 0; i < N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_syscalls); i++)
+    {
+      if (strcmp (name, seccomp_syscalls[i].name) == 0)
+        return seccomp_syscalls[i].nr;
+    }
+
+  die ("Unknown seccomp syscall: %s (use a numeric syscall number for "
+       "syscalls not in bwrap's name table)", name);
+}
+
+static uint32_t
+parse_action (const char *action)
+{
+  uint64_t value;
+
+  if (strcmp (action, "allow") == 0)
+    return SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW;
+  if (strcmp (action, "kill") == 0)
+    return SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS;
+  if (strcmp (action, "trap") == 0)
+    return SECCOMP_RET_TRAP;
+  if (strcmp (action, "log") == 0)
+    return SECCOMP_RET_LOG;
+
+  if (has_prefix (action, "errno:"))
+    {
+      value = parse_constant (action + strlen ("errno:"),
+                              seccomp_errno_constants,
+                              N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_errno_constants),
+                              "errno");
+      if (value > SECCOMP_RET_DATA)
+        die ("Seccomp errno is out of range: %s", action);
+
+      return SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO | (uint32_t) value;
+    }
+
+  die ("Invalid seccomp action: %s (expected allow, kill, trap, log, or "
+       "errno:ERRNO)", action);
+}
+
+static unsigned int
+parse_arg_index (const char *arg)
+{
+  char *end = NULL;
+  unsigned long index;
+
+  if (has_prefix (arg, "arg"))
+    arg += strlen ("arg");
+
+  errno = 0;
+  index = strtoul (arg, &end, 10);
+  if (arg[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' &&
+      errno != ERANGE && index < 6)
+    return (unsigned int) index;
+
+  die ("Invalid seccomp syscall argument: %s (expected arg0 to arg5)",
+       arg);
+}
+
+static void
+seccomp_arg_append (SeccompRule *rule,
+                    SeccompArg  *arg)
+{
+  if (rule->last_arg != NULL)
+    rule->last_arg->next = arg;
+  else
+    rule->args = arg;
+
+  rule->last_arg = arg;
+}
+
+static BpfLabel *
+bpf_label_new (void)
+{
+  return xcalloc (1, sizeof (BpfLabel));
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_label_bind (BpfLabel *label,
+                size_t    offset)
+{
+  if (label->bound)
+    die ("Internal error: seccomp BPF label bound twice");
+
+  label->offset = offset;
+  label->bound = true;
+}
+
+static size_t
+bpf_add (BpfBuilder         *builder,
+         struct sock_filter  instruction)
+{
+  if (builder->len >= BPF_MAXINSNS)
+    die ("Declarative seccomp policy is too large");
+
+  if (builder->len == builder->allocated)
+    {
+      builder->allocated = MAX (builder->allocated * 2, 64);
+      builder->instructions =
+        xrealloc (builder->instructions,
+                  builder->allocated * sizeof (struct sock_filter));
+    }
+
+  builder->instructions[builder->len] = instruction;
+  return builder->len++;
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_add_jump_ref (BpfBuilder *builder,
+                  size_t      instruction,
+                  bool        true_branch,
+                  BpfLabel   *label)
+{
+  BpfJumpRef *ref;
+
+  if (label == NULL)
+    return;
+
+  ref = xcalloc (1, sizeof (BpfJumpRef));
+  ref->instruction = instruction;
+  ref->true_branch = true_branch;
+  ref->label = label;
+  ref->next = builder->jump_refs;
+  builder->jump_refs = ref;
+}
+
+static size_t
+bpf_add_jump (BpfBuilder *builder,
+              uint16_t    code,
+              uint32_t    value,
+              BpfLabel   *true_label,
+              BpfLabel   *false_label)
+{
+  size_t instruction;
+
+  instruction = bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_JUMP (code, value, 0, 0));
+  bpf_add_jump_ref (builder, instruction, true, true_label);
+  bpf_add_jump_ref (builder, instruction, false, false_label);
+  return instruction;
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_load_absolute (BpfBuilder *builder,
+                   size_t      offset)
+{
+  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_LD | BPF_W | BPF_ABS, offset));
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_and_constant (BpfBuilder *builder,
+                  uint32_t    mask)
+{
+  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_ALU | BPF_AND | BPF_K, mask));
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_return (BpfBuilder *builder,
+            uint32_t    action)
+{
+  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_RET | BPF_K, action));
+}
+
+static size_t
+bpf_arg_offset (unsigned int arg,
+                unsigned int word)
+{
+  return offsetof (struct seccomp_data, args[arg]) + word * sizeof (uint32_t);
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_add_arg_predicate (BpfBuilder  *builder,
+                       SeccompArg  *predicate,
+                       BpfLabel    *fail_label)
+{
+  BpfLabel *success_label;
+  uint64_t expected;
+  uint32_t expected_0;
+  uint32_t expected_1;
+  uint32_t mask_0;
+  uint32_t mask_1;
+
+  expected = predicate->value & predicate->mask;
+  expected_0 = ARG_WORD_0 (expected);
+  expected_1 = ARG_WORD_1 (expected);
+  mask_0 = ARG_WORD_0 (predicate->mask);
+  mask_1 = ARG_WORD_1 (predicate->mask);
+
+  success_label = bpf_label_new ();
+
+  bpf_load_absolute (builder, bpf_arg_offset (predicate->index, 0));
+  bpf_and_constant (builder, mask_0);
+  bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, expected_0,
+                NULL,
+                predicate->op == SECCOMP_ARG_EQ ? fail_label : success_label);
+
+  bpf_load_absolute (builder, bpf_arg_offset (predicate->index, 1));
+  bpf_and_constant (builder, mask_1);
+  bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, expected_1,
+                predicate->op == SECCOMP_ARG_EQ ? NULL : fail_label,
+                NULL);
+
+  bpf_label_bind (success_label, builder->len);
+}
+
+static void
+bpf_finish_jumps (BpfBuilder *builder)
+{
+  BpfJumpRef *ref;
+
+  for (ref = builder->jump_refs; ref != NULL; ref = ref->next)
+    {
+      size_t offset;
+
+      if (!ref->label->bound)
+        die ("Internal error: unbound seccomp BPF label");
+
+      if (ref->label->offset < ref->instruction + 1)
+        die ("Internal error: backward seccomp BPF jump");
+
+      offset = ref->label->offset - ref->instruction - 1;
+      if (offset > UINT8_MAX)
+        die ("Declarative seccomp policy is too complex to encode");
+
+      if (ref->true_branch)
+        builder->instructions[ref->instruction].jt = (uint8_t) offset;
+      else
+        builder->instructions[ref->instruction].jf = (uint8_t) offset;
+    }
+}
+
+static bool
+rules_have_same_syscall (SeccompRule *rule,
+                         int          syscall_nr)
+{
+  return rule != NULL && rule->syscall_nr == syscall_nr;
+}
+
+static void
+seccomp_policy_compile_rules (SeccompPolicy *policy,
+                              BpfBuilder    *builder)
+{
+  SeccompRule *rule = policy->rules;
+
+  while (rule != NULL)
+    {
+      BpfLabel *next_group_label = bpf_label_new ();
+      int syscall_nr = rule->syscall_nr;
+
+      bpf_load_absolute (builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, nr));
+      bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, syscall_nr,
+                    NULL, next_group_label);
+
+      while (rules_have_same_syscall (rule, syscall_nr))
+        {
+          BpfLabel *next_rule_label = bpf_label_new ();
+          SeccompArg *arg;
+
+          for (arg = rule->args; arg != NULL; arg = arg->next)
+            bpf_add_arg_predicate (builder, arg, next_rule_label);
+
+          bpf_return (builder, rule->action);
+          bpf_label_bind (next_rule_label, builder->len);
+          rule = rule->next;
+        }
+
+      bpf_label_bind (next_group_label, builder->len);
+    }
+}
+
+SeccompPolicy *
+seccomp_policy_new (void)
+{
+  SeccompPolicy *policy = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompPolicy));
+
+  policy->default_action = SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW;
+  return policy;
+}
+
+void
+seccomp_policy_free (SeccompPolicy *policy)
+{
+  SeccompRule *rule;
+  SeccompRule *next_rule;
+
+  if (policy == NULL)
+    return;
+
+  for (rule = policy->rules; rule != NULL; rule = next_rule)
+    {
+      SeccompArg *arg;
+      SeccompArg *next_arg;
+
+      next_rule = rule->next;
+      for (arg = rule->args; arg != NULL; arg = next_arg)
+        {
+          next_arg = arg->next;
+          free (arg);
+        }
+      free (rule);
+    }
+
+  free (policy);
+}
+
+void
+seccomp_policy_set_default_action (SeccompPolicy *policy,
+                                   const char    *action)
+{
+  policy->default_action = parse_action (action);
+  policy->has_default_action = true;
+}
+
+void
+seccomp_policy_add_rule (SeccompPolicy *policy,
+                         const char    *spec)
+{
+  cleanup_free char *copy = xstrdup (spec);
+  char *saveptr = NULL;
+  char *action_token;
+  char *syscall_token;
+  char *arg_token;
+  SeccompRule *rule;
+
+  action_token = strtok_r (copy, " \t", &saveptr);
+  if (action_token == NULL)
+    die ("Empty --seccomp-rule");
+
+  syscall_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
+  if (syscall_token == NULL)
+    die ("--seccomp-rule requires a syscall name");
+
+  rule = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompRule));
+  rule->action = parse_action (action_token);
+  rule->syscall_nr = parse_syscall (syscall_token);
+
+  while ((arg_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr)) != NULL)
+    {
+      SeccompArg *arg = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompArg));
+      char *operator_token;
+      char *value_token;
+
+      arg->index = parse_arg_index (arg_token);
+      arg->mask = UINT64_MAX;
+
+      operator_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
+      if (operator_token == NULL)
+        die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing an operator", arg_token);
+
+      if (strcmp (operator_token, "&") == 0)
+        {
+          char *mask_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
+
+          if (mask_token == NULL)
+            die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a mask", arg_token);
+
+          arg->mask = parse_constant (mask_token,
+                                      seccomp_value_constants,
+                                      N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_value_constants),
+                                      "mask");
+
+          operator_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
+          if (operator_token == NULL)
+            die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a comparison",
+                 arg_token);
+        }
+
+      if (strcmp (operator_token, "==") == 0)
+        arg->op = SECCOMP_ARG_EQ;
+      else if (strcmp (operator_token, "!=") == 0)
+        arg->op = SECCOMP_ARG_NE;
+      else
+        die ("Invalid seccomp argument operator: %s (expected == or !=)",
+             operator_token);
+
+      value_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
+      if (value_token == NULL)
+        die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a value", arg_token);
+
+      arg->value = parse_constant (value_token,
+                                   seccomp_value_constants,
+                                   N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_value_constants),
+                                   "value");
+      seccomp_arg_append (rule, arg);
+    }
+
+  if (policy->last_rule != NULL)
+    policy->last_rule->next = rule;
+  else
+    policy->rules = rule;
+
+  policy->last_rule = rule;
+}
+
+struct sock_fprog *
+seccomp_policy_compile (SeccompPolicy *policy)
+{
+  BpfBuilder builder = { 0 };
+  BpfLabel *wrong_arch_label;
+  struct sock_fprog *program;
+
+  bpf_load_absolute (&builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, arch));
+  wrong_arch_label = bpf_label_new ();
+  bpf_add_jump (&builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K,
+                BWRAP_SECCOMP_AUDIT_ARCH, NULL, wrong_arch_label);
+
+#if defined(__x86_64__)
+  bpf_load_absolute (&builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, nr));
+  bpf_add_jump (&builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JSET | BPF_K, 0x40000000,
+                wrong_arch_label, NULL);
+#endif
+
+  seccomp_policy_compile_rules (policy, &builder);
+  bpf_return (&builder, policy->default_action);
+  bpf_label_bind (wrong_arch_label, builder.len);
+  bpf_return (&builder, SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO | ENOSYS);
+
+  bpf_finish_jumps (&builder);
+
+  program = xcalloc (1, sizeof (struct sock_fprog));
+  program->len = builder.len;
+  program->filter = builder.instructions;
+  return program;
+}

typedef struct _BpfLabel BpfLabel;
typedef struct _BpfJumpRef BpfJumpRef;
typedef struct _BpfBuilder BpfBuilder;

struct _BpfLabel
{
  size_t offset;
  bool   bound;
};

struct _BpfJumpRef
{
  size_t       instruction;
  bool         true_branch;
  BpfLabel    *label;
  BpfJumpRef  *next;
};

struct _BpfBuilder
{
  struct sock_filter *instructions;
  size_t              len;
  size_t              allocated;
  BpfJumpRef         *jump_refs;
};

static uint64_t
parse_constant (const char               *value,
                const SeccompConstant    *constants,
                size_t                    n_constants,
                const char               *description)
{
  char *end = NULL;
  unsigned long long parsed;
  size_t i;

  errno = 0;
  parsed = strtoull (value, &end, 0);
  if (value[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' && errno != ERANGE)
    return parsed;

  for (i = 0; i < n_constants; i++)
    {
      if (strcmp (value, constants[i].name) == 0)
        return constants[i].value;
    }

  die ("Invalid seccomp %s: %s", description, value);
}

static int
parse_syscall (const char *name)
{
  char *end = NULL;
  unsigned long parsed;
  size_t i;

  errno = 0;
  parsed = strtoul (name, &end, 0);
  if (name[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' &&
      errno != ERANGE && parsed <= INT_MAX)
    return (int) parsed;

  for (i = 0; i < N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_syscalls); i++)
    {
      if (strcmp (name, seccomp_syscalls[i].name) == 0)
        return seccomp_syscalls[i].nr;
    }

  die ("Unknown seccomp syscall: %s (use a numeric syscall number for "
       "syscalls not in bwrap's name table)", name);
}

static uint32_t
parse_action (const char *action)
{
  uint64_t value;

  if (strcmp (action, "allow") == 0)
    return SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW;
  if (strcmp (action, "kill") == 0)
    return SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS;
  if (strcmp (action, "trap") == 0)
    return SECCOMP_RET_TRAP;
  if (strcmp (action, "log") == 0)
    return SECCOMP_RET_LOG;

  if (has_prefix (action, "errno:"))
    {
      value = parse_constant (action + strlen ("errno:"),
                              seccomp_errno_constants,
                              N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_errno_constants),
                              "errno");
      if (value > SECCOMP_RET_DATA)
        die ("Seccomp errno is out of range: %s", action);

      return SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO | (uint32_t) value;
    }

  die ("Invalid seccomp action: %s (expected allow, kill, trap, log, or "
       "errno:ERRNO)", action);
}

static unsigned int
parse_arg_index (const char *arg)
{
  char *end = NULL;
  unsigned long index;

  if (has_prefix (arg, "arg"))
    arg += strlen ("arg");

  errno = 0;
  index = strtoul (arg, &end, 10);
  if (arg[0] != '\0' && end != NULL && end[0] == '\0' &&
      errno != ERANGE && index < 6)
    return (unsigned int) index;

  die ("Invalid seccomp syscall argument: %s (expected arg0 to arg5)",
       arg);
}

static void
seccomp_arg_append (SeccompRule *rule,
                    SeccompArg  *arg)
{
  if (rule->last_arg != NULL)
    rule->last_arg->next = arg;
  else
    rule->args = arg;

  rule->last_arg = arg;
}

static BpfLabel *
bpf_label_new (void)
{
  return xcalloc (1, sizeof (BpfLabel));
}

static void
bpf_label_bind (BpfLabel *label,
                size_t    offset)
{
  if (label->bound)
    die ("Internal error: seccomp BPF label bound twice");

  label->offset = offset;
  label->bound = true;
}

static size_t
bpf_add (BpfBuilder         *builder,
         struct sock_filter  instruction)
{
  if (builder->len >= BPF_MAXINSNS)
    die ("Declarative seccomp policy is too large");

  if (builder->len == builder->allocated)
    {
      builder->allocated = MAX (builder->allocated * 2, 64);
      builder->instructions =
        xrealloc (builder->instructions,
                  builder->allocated * sizeof (struct sock_filter));
    }

  builder->instructions[builder->len] = instruction;
  return builder->len++;
}

static void
bpf_add_jump_ref (BpfBuilder *builder,
                  size_t      instruction,
                  bool        true_branch,
                  BpfLabel   *label)
{
  BpfJumpRef *ref;

  if (label == NULL)
    return;

  ref = xcalloc (1, sizeof (BpfJumpRef));
  ref->instruction = instruction;
  ref->true_branch = true_branch;
  ref->label = label;
  ref->next = builder->jump_refs;
  builder->jump_refs = ref;
}

static size_t
bpf_add_jump (BpfBuilder *builder,
              uint16_t    code,
              uint32_t    value,
              BpfLabel   *true_label,
              BpfLabel   *false_label)
{
  size_t instruction;

  instruction = bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_JUMP (code, value, 0, 0));
  bpf_add_jump_ref (builder, instruction, true, true_label);
  bpf_add_jump_ref (builder, instruction, false, false_label);
  return instruction;
}

static void
bpf_load_absolute (BpfBuilder *builder,
                   size_t      offset)
{
  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_LD | BPF_W | BPF_ABS, offset));
}

static void
bpf_and_constant (BpfBuilder *builder,
                  uint32_t    mask)
{
  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_ALU | BPF_AND | BPF_K, mask));
}

static void
bpf_return (BpfBuilder *builder,
            uint32_t    action)
{
  bpf_add (builder, (struct sock_filter) BPF_STMT (BPF_RET | BPF_K, action));
}

static size_t
bpf_arg_offset (unsigned int arg,
                unsigned int word)
{
  return offsetof (struct seccomp_data, args[arg]) + word * sizeof (uint32_t);
}

static void
bpf_add_arg_predicate (BpfBuilder  *builder,
                       SeccompArg  *predicate,
                       BpfLabel    *fail_label)
{
  BpfLabel *success_label;
  uint64_t expected;
  uint32_t expected_0;
  uint32_t expected_1;
  uint32_t mask_0;
  uint32_t mask_1;

  expected = predicate->value & predicate->mask;
  expected_0 = ARG_WORD_0 (expected);
  expected_1 = ARG_WORD_1 (expected);
  mask_0 = ARG_WORD_0 (predicate->mask);
  mask_1 = ARG_WORD_1 (predicate->mask);

  success_label = bpf_label_new ();

  bpf_load_absolute (builder, bpf_arg_offset (predicate->index, 0));
  bpf_and_constant (builder, mask_0);
  bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, expected_0,
                NULL,
                predicate->op == SECCOMP_ARG_EQ ? fail_label : success_label);

  bpf_load_absolute (builder, bpf_arg_offset (predicate->index, 1));
  bpf_and_constant (builder, mask_1);
  bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, expected_1,
                predicate->op == SECCOMP_ARG_EQ ? NULL : fail_label,
                NULL);

  bpf_label_bind (success_label, builder->len);
}

static void
bpf_finish_jumps (BpfBuilder *builder)
{
  BpfJumpRef *ref;

  for (ref = builder->jump_refs; ref != NULL; ref = ref->next)
    {
      size_t offset;

      if (!ref->label->bound)
        die ("Internal error: unbound seccomp BPF label");

      if (ref->label->offset < ref->instruction + 1)
        die ("Internal error: backward seccomp BPF jump");

      offset = ref->label->offset - ref->instruction - 1;
      if (offset > UINT8_MAX)
        die ("Declarative seccomp policy is too complex to encode");

      if (ref->true_branch)
        builder->instructions[ref->instruction].jt = (uint8_t) offset;
      else
        builder->instructions[ref->instruction].jf = (uint8_t) offset;
    }
}

static bool
rules_have_same_syscall (SeccompRule *rule,
                         int          syscall_nr)
{
  return rule != NULL && rule->syscall_nr == syscall_nr;
}

static void
seccomp_policy_compile_rules (SeccompPolicy *policy,
                              BpfBuilder    *builder)
{
  SeccompRule *rule = policy->rules;

  while (rule != NULL)
    {
      BpfLabel *next_group_label = bpf_label_new ();
      int syscall_nr = rule->syscall_nr;

      bpf_load_absolute (builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, nr));
      bpf_add_jump (builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, syscall_nr,
                    NULL, next_group_label);

      while (rules_have_same_syscall (rule, syscall_nr))
        {
          BpfLabel *next_rule_label = bpf_label_new ();
          SeccompArg *arg;

          for (arg = rule->args; arg != NULL; arg = arg->next)
            bpf_add_arg_predicate (builder, arg, next_rule_label);

          bpf_return (builder, rule->action);
          bpf_label_bind (next_rule_label, builder->len);
          rule = rule->next;
        }

      bpf_label_bind (next_group_label, builder->len);
    }
}

SeccompPolicy *
seccomp_policy_new (void)
{
  SeccompPolicy *policy = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompPolicy));

  policy->default_action = SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW;
  return policy;
}

void
seccomp_policy_free (SeccompPolicy *policy)
{
  SeccompRule *rule;
  SeccompRule *next_rule;

  if (policy == NULL)
    return;

  for (rule = policy->rules; rule != NULL; rule = next_rule)
    {
      SeccompArg *arg;
      SeccompArg *next_arg;

      next_rule = rule->next;
      for (arg = rule->args; arg != NULL; arg = next_arg)
        {
          next_arg = arg->next;
          free (arg);
        }
      free (rule);
    }

  free (policy);
}

void
seccomp_policy_set_default_action (SeccompPolicy *policy,
                                   const char    *action)
{
  policy->default_action = parse_action (action);
  policy->has_default_action = true;
}

void
seccomp_policy_add_rule (SeccompPolicy *policy,
                         const char    *spec)
{
  cleanup_free char *copy = xstrdup (spec);
  char *saveptr = NULL;
  char *action_token;
  char *syscall_token;
  char *arg_token;
  SeccompRule *rule;

  action_token = strtok_r (copy, " \t", &saveptr);
  if (action_token == NULL)
    die ("Empty --seccomp-rule");

  syscall_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
  if (syscall_token == NULL)
    die ("--seccomp-rule requires a syscall name");

  rule = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompRule));
  rule->action = parse_action (action_token);
  rule->syscall_nr = parse_syscall (syscall_token);

  while ((arg_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr)) != NULL)
    {
      SeccompArg *arg = xcalloc (1, sizeof (SeccompArg));
      char *operator_token;
      char *value_token;

      arg->index = parse_arg_index (arg_token);
      arg->mask = UINT64_MAX;

      operator_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
      if (operator_token == NULL)
        die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing an operator", arg_token);

      if (strcmp (operator_token, "&") == 0)
        {
          char *mask_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);

          if (mask_token == NULL)
            die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a mask", arg_token);

          arg->mask = parse_constant (mask_token,
                                      seccomp_value_constants,
                                      N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_value_constants),
                                      "mask");

          operator_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
          if (operator_token == NULL)
            die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a comparison",
                 arg_token);
        }

      if (strcmp (operator_token, "==") == 0)
        arg->op = SECCOMP_ARG_EQ;
      else if (strcmp (operator_token, "!=") == 0)
        arg->op = SECCOMP_ARG_NE;
      else
        die ("Invalid seccomp argument operator: %s (expected == or !=)",
             operator_token);

      value_token = strtok_r (NULL, " \t", &saveptr);
      if (value_token == NULL)
        die ("--seccomp-rule argument %s is missing a value", arg_token);

      arg->value = parse_constant (value_token,
                                   seccomp_value_constants,
                                   N_ELEMENTS (seccomp_value_constants),
                                   "value");
      seccomp_arg_append (rule, arg);
    }

  if (policy->last_rule != NULL)
    policy->last_rule->next = rule;
  else
    policy->rules = rule;

  policy->last_rule = rule;
}

struct sock_fprog *
seccomp_policy_compile (SeccompPolicy *policy)
{
  BpfBuilder builder = { 0 };
  BpfLabel *wrong_arch_label;
  struct sock_fprog *program;

  bpf_load_absolute (&builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, arch));
  wrong_arch_label = bpf_label_new ();
  bpf_add_jump (&builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K,
                BWRAP_SECCOMP_AUDIT_ARCH, NULL, wrong_arch_label);

#if defined(__x86_64__)
  bpf_load_absolute (&builder, offsetof (struct seccomp_data, nr));
  bpf_add_jump (&builder, BPF_JMP | BPF_JSET | BPF_K, 0x40000000,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.1-or-later

import errno
import logging
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import termios
import unittest


TIOCSTI = getattr(termios, 'TIOCSTI', None)
TIOCNOTTY = getattr(termios, 'TIOCNOTTY', None)


class Test(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

        if 'G_TEST_SRCDIR' in os.environ:
            self.test_srcdir = os.getenv('G_TEST_SRCDIR') + '/tests'
        else:
            self.test_srcdir = here

        if 'G_TEST_BUILDDIR' in os.environ:
            self.test_builddir = os.getenv('G_TEST_BUILDDIR') + '/tests'
        else:
            self.test_builddir = here

        self.bwrap = os.getenv('BWRAP', 'bwrap')
        self.try_syscall = os.path.join(self.test_builddir, 'try-syscall')

        if TIOCSTI is None or TIOCNOTTY is None:
            self.skipTest('TIOCSTI/TIOCNOTTY are not available')

        completed = subprocess.run(
            [
                self.bwrap,
                '--ro-bind', '/', '/',
                'true',
            ],
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=2,
        )

        if completed.returncode != 0:
            raise unittest.SkipTest(
                'cannot run bwrap (does it need to be setuid?)'
            )

    def run_syscall(self, syscall, *options):
        return subprocess.run(
            [
                self.bwrap,
                '--ro-bind', '/', '/',
                *options,
                self.try_syscall, syscall,
            ],
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )

    def assert_syscall_errno(self, syscall, expected, *options):
        completed = self.run_syscall(syscall, *options)
        self.assertEqual(
            completed.returncode,
            expected,
            completed.stderr.decode(errors='replace'),
        )

    def test_argument_eq(self) -> None:
        rule = 'errno:ECONNREFUSED ioctl arg1 == 0x{:x}'.format(TIOCSTI)

        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCSTI', errno.ECONNREFUSED,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )
        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCNOTTY', errno.EBADF,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )

    def test_argument_masked_eq(self) -> None:
        rule = 'errno:ECONNREFUSED ioctl arg1 & 0xffffffff == TIOCSTI'

        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCSTI', errno.ECONNREFUSED,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )

        completed = self.run_syscall(
            'ioctl TIOCSTI CVE-2019-10063',
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )
        if completed.returncode == errno.ENOENT:
            print('# Cannot test 64-bit syscall parameter on 32-bit')
        else:
            self.assertEqual(
                completed.returncode,
                errno.ECONNREFUSED,
                completed.stderr.decode(errors='replace'),
            )

        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCNOTTY', errno.EBADF,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )

    def test_argument_ne(self) -> None:
        rule = 'errno:ECONNREFUSED ioctl arg1 != TIOCNOTTY'

        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCSTI', errno.ECONNREFUSED,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )
        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCNOTTY', errno.EBADF,
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )

    def test_syscall_without_arguments(self) -> None:
        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'listen', errno.ECONNREFUSED,
            '--seccomp-rule', 'errno:ECONNREFUSED listen',
        )
        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCNOTTY', errno.EBADF,
            '--seccomp-rule', 'errno:ECONNREFUSED listen',
        )

    def test_namespace_combination(self) -> None:
        rule = 'errno:ECONNREFUSED ioctl arg1 == TIOCSTI'

        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCSTI', errno.ECONNREFUSED,
            '--unshare-user-try',
            '--unshare-pid',
            '--unshare-ipc',
            '--unshare-uts',
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )
        self.assert_syscall_errno(
            'ioctl TIOCNOTTY', errno.EBADF,
            '--unshare-user-try',
            '--unshare-pid',
            '--unshare-ipc',
            '--unshare-uts',
            '--seccomp-rule', rule,
        )

    def test_invalid_rules(self) -> None:
        invalid_rules = [
            'deny read',
            'errno:EPERM',
            'errno:EPERM not-a-syscall',
            'errno:EPERM ioctl arg6 == 0',
            'errno:EPERM ioctl arg0 = 0',
            'errno:EPERM ioctl arg0 & 0xff',
            'errno:EPERM ioctl arg0 & 0xff ~ 0',
        ]

        for rule in invalid_rules:
            with self.subTest(rule=rule):
                completed = subprocess.run(
                    [
                        self.bwrap,
                        '--ro-bind', '/', '/',
                        '--seccomp-rule', rule,
                        'true',
                    ],
                    stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                )
                self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)
                self.assertIn(b'bwrap: ', completed.stderr)


def main():
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

    try:
        from tap.runner import TAPTestRunner
    except ImportError:
        TAPTestRunner = None    # type: ignore

    if TAPTestRunner is not None:
        runner = TAPTestRunner()
        runner.set_stream(True)
        unittest.main(testRunner=runner)
    else:
        print('# tap.runner not available, using simple TAP output')
        print('1..1')
        program = unittest.main(exit=False)
        if program.result.wasSuccessful():
            print('ok 1 - %r' % program.result)
        else:
            print('not ok 1 - %r' % program.result)
            sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

This is an incomplete example, but useful for purposes of
illustration.  More often, rather than creating a container using the
host's filesystem tree, you want to target a chroot.  There, rather
than creating the symlink `lib64 -> usr/lib64` in the tmpfs, you might
have already created it in the target rootfs.

Sandboxing
----------

The goal of bubblewrap is to run an application in a sandbox, where it
has restricted access to parts of the operating system or user data
such as the home directory.

bubblewrap always creates a new mount namespace, and the user can specify
exactly what parts of the filesystem should be visible in the sandbox.
Any such directories you specify mounted `nodev` by default, and can be made readonly.

Additionally you can use these kernel features:

User namespaces ([CLONE_NEWUSER](https://linux.die.net/man/2/clone)): This hides all but the current uid and gid from the
sandbox. You can also change what the value of uid/gid should be in the sandbox.

IPC namespaces ([CLONE_NEWIPC](https://linux.die.net/man/2/clone)): The sandbox will get its own copy of all the
different forms of IPCs, like SysV shared memory and semaphores.

PID namespaces ([CLONE_NEWPID](https://linux.die.net/man/2/clone)): The sandbox will not see any processes outside the sandbox. Additionally, bubblewrap will run a trivial pid1 inside your container to handle the requirements of reaping children in the sandbox. This avoids what is known now as the [Docker pid 1 problem](https://blog.phusion.nl/docker-and-the-pid-1-zombie-reaping-problem/).


Network namespaces ([CLONE_NEWNET](https://linux.die.net/man/2/clone)): The sandbox will not see the network. Instead it will have its own network namespace with only a loopback device.

UTS namespace ([CLONE_NEWUTS](https://linux.die.net/man/2/clone)): The sandbox will have its own hostname.

Seccomp filters: You can pass in seccomp filters that limit which syscalls can be done in the sandbox. For more information, see [Seccomp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seccomp).

Limitations
-----------

As noted in the [Sandbox security](#sandbox-security) section above,
the level of protection between the sandboxed processes and the host system
is entirely determined by the arguments passed to bubblewrap.
Some aspects that require special care are noted here.

- If you are not filtering out `TIOCSTI` commands using seccomp filters,
argument `--new-session` is needed to protect against out-of-sandbox
command execution
(see [CVE-2017-5226](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/issues/142)).

- Everything mounted into the sandbox can potentially be used to escalate
privileges.
For example, if you bind a D-Bus socket into the sandbox, it can be used to
execute commands via systemd. You can use
[xdg-dbus-proxy](https://github.com/flatpak/xdg-dbus-proxy) to filter
D-Bus communication.

- Some applications deploy their own sandboxing mechanisms, and these can be
restricted by the constraints imposed by bubblewrap's sandboxing.
For example, some web browsers which configure their child proccesses via
seccomp to not have access to the filesystem. If you limit the syscalls and
don't allow the seccomp syscall, a browser cannot apply these restrictions.
Similarly, if these rules were compiled into a file that is not available in
the sandbox, the browser cannot load these rules from this file and cannot
apply these restrictions.

Related project comparison: Firejail
------------------------------------

[Firejail](https://github.com/netblue30/firejail/tree/HEAD/src/firejail)
is similar to Flatpak before bubblewrap was split out in that it combines
a setuid tool with a lot of desktop-specific sandboxing features.  For
example, Firejail knows about Pulseaudio, whereas bubblewrap does not.


The bubblewrap authors believe it's much easier to audit a small
setuid program, and keep features such as Pulseaudio filtering as an
unprivileged process, as now occurs in Flatpak.

Also, @cgwalters thinks trying to
[whitelist file paths](https://github.com/netblue30/firejail/blob/37a5a3545ef6d8d03dad8bbd888f53e13274c9e5/src/firejail/fs_whitelist.c#L176)
is a bad idea given the myriad ways users have to manipulate paths,
and the myriad ways in which system administrators may configure a
system.  The bubblewrap approach is to only retain a few specific
Linux capabilities such as `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, but to always access the
filesystem as the invoking uid.  This entirely closes
[TOCTTOU attacks](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/367.html) and
such.

Related project comparison: Sandstorm.io
----------------------------------------

[Sandstorm.io](https://sandstorm.io/) requires unprivileged user
namespaces to set up its sandbox, though it could easily be adapted
to operate in a setuid mode as well. @cgwalters believes their code is
fairly good, but it could still make sense to unify on bubblewrap.
However, @kentonv (of Sandstorm) feels that while this makes sense
in principle, the switching cost outweighs the practical benefits for
now. This decision could be re-evaluated in the future, but it is not
being actively pursued today.

Related project comparison: runc/binctr
----------------------------------------

[runC](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc) is currently working on
supporting [rootless containers](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/774),
without needing `setuid` or any other privileges during installation of
runC (using unprivileged user namespaces rather than `setuid`),
creation, and management of containers. However, the standard mode of
using runC is similar to [systemd nspawn](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd-nspawn.html)
in that it is tooling intended to be invoked by root.

The bubblewrap authors believe that runc and systemd-nspawn are not
designed to be made setuid, and are distant from supporting such a mode.
However with rootless containers, runC will be able to fulfill certain usecases
that bubblewrap supports (with the added benefit of being a standardised and
complete OCI runtime).

[binctr](https://github.com/jfrazelle/binctr) is just a wrapper for
runC, so inherits all of its design tradeoffs.

What's with the name?!
----------------------

content.text:
**实现**
- 新增可重复的 `--seccomp-rule 'ACTION SYSCALL [argN OP VALUE]...'`，支持 `==`、`!=`、位掩码 `arg1 & 0xffffffff == TIOCSTI`、命名常量和数值 syscall。
- 新增 `--seccomp-default`，用于配置未匹配 syscall 的默认动作，默认 `allow`。
- 在 `seccomp.c` 中实现规则解析及 cBPF 生成，包含架构校验和 64 位参数比较；与 `--unshare-*`、原始 BPF 过滤器可组合，过滤器在 namespace 建立后、exec 前安装。
- 更新了帮助、man page、README、NEWS 和 bash/zsh 补全。
- 示例：
  ```sh
  bwrap --unshare-all --ro-bind / / \
    --seccomp-rule 'errno:EPERM ioctl arg1 == TIOCSTI' \
    COMMAND
  ```

核心代码见 `seccomp.c:1154`、`seccomp.c:1235` 和 `bubblewrap.c:2444`；文档见 `bwrap.xml:517`。

**验证**
- 新增 `tests/test-seccomp-args.py:74`，覆盖参数等值、掩码、`!=`、多规则、无参数规则、namespace 组合及非法输入。
- `test-utils`、`test-seccomp-args.py`、`test-specifying-pidns.sh`、`test-specifying-userns.sh`、`test-sandbox.py` 均通过；ASAN/UBSAN 构建下新测试也通过。
- `test-seccomp.py` 因环境缺少 `python3-seccomp` 跳过。
- 完整套件中的 `test-run.sh` 在 `--file 0` 处 SIGABRT；已用未修改的基线版本复现，确认是当前 WSL 环境问题，与本次改动无关。
